title: Remarks to the Veterans Who Escorted Him to the Dock, Oakland
occasion: To the veterans who escorted him to the dock
paragraphs: My Comrades of the Great War:

I wish to thank you for the privilege. These are the only bodies of men to whom it gives me even greater pleasure to pay greeting than to my own comrades of the lesser war. Pleased though I was to have the service men of the war parade as my escort, looking so familiar in the uniform that I knew so well, yet it is an even greater pleasure to be greeted by you whose example we endeavored to follow, and the memories of whose deeds must forever be to all Americans a source of inspiration to duty, whether it be in war or in peace. (Cheers and applause.)
